 Calvin Harris Announces His First Ever Headlining North American Tour: Is He Coming to Your City?
 The tour announcement comes after billboards teasing the run appeared across North America last week. 
 By
 Katie Bain

 After billboards teasing shows by Calvin Harris appeared in cities including Chicago, New York, Houston, Vancouver and San Diego last week, the Scottish producer has today (Oct. 13) announced his first headlining North American tour.
 While the superstar producer has played major venues and festivals across the country, the 18-date arena tour will be the first full headlining North American tour of his career. 
 Related

 Calvin Harris Spins His Way Into Guinness World Records 
 Produced by Live Nation, the run begins April 1, 2027, in Boston and extends through May 27, when the tour wraps at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. See the complete tour dates below. A general ticket on sale begins Oct. 22 at noon PT.
 The announcement comes after a particularly big few weeks for Harris, who last month earned a Guinness World Record for the largest attendance for a DJ set by a single artist. The record was set in February, when Harris performed for an estimated 1.6 million people in São Paulo, Brazil. This past weekend, he performed as part of Head Trip, the one-time-only dance festival produced by Goldenvoice on the Coachella grounds in Indio, Calif.
 This performance saw Harris pulling from his arsenal of era-defining hits, with the show including “Feel So Close,” “Sweet Nothing,” “How Deep Is Your Love” and “We Found Love,” all songs that will surely be part of the setlist for the just-announced arena run. Harris has earned 22 Hot 100 hits, including one No. 1. 
 The tour is another signal of dance’s music current popularity in the U.S., with the 2026 Luminate mid-year report citing it as the fastest-growing genre.
